children.translated_text: For whoever finds union with things dear, for that very person separation from those same things—how could it not be painful? children.translated_text: For the eminent, suffering is mental; for the rest, it is physical.

One might think: Even though suffering exists, it is not unrecognized as a source of harm. For some are seen to be exclusively happy from birth until death. And those of the highest status, established in great positions, do not feel [suffering] due to their absorption in that. How then can the body be said to be of the nature of suffering? It is said:
The mental suffering belongs to the eminent; for the rest, it arises from the body.
By this twofold suffering, this world is struck day after day.

m uparundhyād ity ataḥ sukhavan na duḥkhaṃ kalpanāvaśyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, unlike happiness, suffering is not under the control of imagination.

When indeed a person imagines thus: 'I am a giver, I am a lord, I enjoy desirable sense objects'—then, as he thus imagines, mental happiness arises. But even for those to whom happiness is offered, fearing the loss of that from others, through the imagination of the cessation of enjoyment, that mental happiness ceases again. Thus, since both the arising and cessation of happiness are subject to imagination, happiness is under the control of imagination. But suffering is not like that. For there is no imagination whatsoever that has the power to obstruct the capacity of suffering to harm.

children.text: yat tu khalv idam iṣṭaviṣayasambhogasukhaṃ yā ca sukhodayānukūlā kalpanā tad ubhayam api duḥkham upajātam upahanti / tathā hīndriyārtham upabhuñjāno 'py ayam anyatamena duḥkhenābhibhūtaḥ saha kalpanayā tat sarvaṃ sukham apahāya duḥkham eva pratisaṃvitte

Furthermore, this happiness of enjoying desirable objects, and the imagination favorable to the arising of happiness—both of these are destroyed by suffering when it arises. For even while enjoying sense objects, this person, overwhelmed by some suffering, along with imagination, abandons all that happiness and perceives only suffering.

When asked, 'Why do you grieve for a beloved who is dead?', she replied, 'I do not grieve for him. Rather, I [grieve] because the co-wife's son lives.' At a later time, when the co-wife's son fell ill, she went to another village. After a few days, she approached that village, and a corpse was being carried out from it. She imagined, 'That very co-wife's son has died.'

Whatever is <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned) and arisen through <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) is impermanent, because of its momentariness. Whatever is impermanent is impure, because it causes alarm. Whatever is impure is suffering, because it causes affliction. And whatever is suffering is without self, because it is not autonomous. Thus, in a single entity, in brief, the four non-inversions occur. But even though this is so, childish beings who are inverted do not discern it. They imagine the opposite qualities in things. children.translated_text: It is replied: Since consciousness is accepted as belonging to the immensely vast <s>puruṣa</s> — vast like space — only in connection with the mind alone, is it not the case that, according to you:

children.translated_text: If, according to your conception, I were all-pervading, pervading everything like space, then, since my self would exist in other beings as well, why would the ego-sense of that [other being] not arise regarding my self in that [other being]? For its all-pervasiveness would be tenable only if the other too had ego-sense regarding my self. And it is not proper that another's self should obstruct my self in another's body, for there is no absence of our self in the region of another's self,

children.text: yadā ca samānadeśatā tadā na tena tasyāvaraṇaṃ śakyaṃ kartum iti pratipādayann āha //
children.translated_text: And since there is co-location, it is not possible for one to obstruct the other — demonstrating this, [the master] says:
What is called 'obstruction' of that [other self] by that very [self co-located with it] is simply untenable.
Thus.
just as

Due to co-location,

children.translated_text: Those <s>guṇas</s> to which agency is attributed, and which are unconscious in every respect—

Namely:
From <s>prakṛti</s> arises <s>mahat</s> (the great principle).
<s>Mahat</s> is a synonym for <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). From <s>mahat</s> arises <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle).
And that is threefold:
<s>sāttvika</s>, <s>rājasa</s>, and <s>tāmasa</s>.

children.text: tatra sāttvikād ahaṅkārāt pañcabuddhīndriyāṇi śrotraṃ tvak cakṣū rasanaṃ ghrāṇam iti / pañcakarmendriyāṇi vāk pāṇi pāda pāyūpasthākhyāni / ubhayātmakaṃ ca mana ity ekādaśa pravartante /
children.translated_text: From the <s>sāttvika ahaṅkāra</s> arise the five <s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s> (cognitive sense organs): hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell; the five <s>karmendriyāṇi</s> (action organs): speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals; and the mind, which partakes of both natures — thus eleven [principles] proceed.

One who possesses action is not eternal.

children.text: si / tathā hi / tasyānāgatabhāvacyutyā hetupratyayair vartamānatā bhavati / na caivam asaṃskṛtaṃ svarūpāt pracyavata iti nāsyāsaṃskṛtavan nityatvam iti / evam api kal

children.translated_text: is not reasonable. For if it had existence, then there would be the birth again of what already exists and is present.

children.text: na ca sataḥ punar api janma nyāyyaṃ niḥprayojanatvāt
children.translated_text: But the birth again of what [already] exists is not reasonable, because it is purposeless.
Because of the undesirable consequence

children.text: ā saṃsāram ekasyaivārthasya punar utpādenāparisamāptodayasya satas tatpadārthāntarāpravṛtter hetuphalabhāvavyāghāta
children.translated_text: that throughout <s>saṃsāra</s>, through the repeated production of one and the same entity whose arising is never completed, there being no functioning of other entities, there would be a contradiction of the cause-effect relationship.

children.text: asti ceyaṃ hetuphalabhūtānāṃ padārthānāṃ santānānuvṛttir iti na yukto 'nāgatapadārthasadbhāvasya vādaḥ /
children.translated_text: And there is this continuity of the succession of entities that are causes and effects — therefore the doctrine of the existence of future entities is not reasonable.
That entity whose production, i.e., coming-into-being, is effected through causes and conditions — that it exists even before
does not

children.text: ṃ na syād yad etad anāgatārthālambanaṃ yogināṃ praṇidhijñānaṃ yathārthaṃ na syāt / asti caitad yathārthaṃ yogināṃ jñānam
children.translated_text: exist, then the resolution-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>) of <s>yogins</s>, which has future objects as its referent, would not be veridical. But this knowledge of <s>yogins</s> is indeed veridical,
because of the prediction of future objects as they truly are, and because those [predictions] come to be exactly so.

children.text: na hy asatsu vandhyāputrādiṣv etat sambhavati
children.translated_text: For this does not occur with regard to non-existents such as a barren woman's son.

children.text: tasmād asty evānāgata iti / ucyate / tāttvikayā kalpanayā
children.translated_text: Therefore, the future does indeed exist. It is replied: by a true analysis —
Here one objects: if the future
if a future entity is seen, why is a non-existent not seen?

children.text: utpādāt prāgavasthāyām anāgato bhāvo nāsti svarūpata iti pratipāditam / yadi cā

children.translated_text: a non-

children.text: dyamānaḥ padārtho yogibhir dṛśyeta vandhyāputrādayo 'pi dṛśyeran / dvayor api tulyaṃ svabhāvāsattvaṃ tatraiko dṛśyate netara iti na yujyate /
children.translated_text: existent entity were seen by <s>yogins</s>, then a barren woman's son and such would also be seen. Since both equally lack inherent existence, it is not reasonable that one is seen and not the other.
It has been established that in the state prior to arising, the future entity does not exist by its own nature. And if

children.text: kiṃ punar yogino 'nāgataṃ nekṣante / yathā bhavān parikalpayati tathā nekṣante / yathābhūtenānāgatenārthena vartamānāvasthena bhavitavyam / teṣāṃ praṇidhibalākṣiptasamādhiviśe
ṣāt tu jñānam utpadyamānaṃ tathā padārthākāraṃ parikalpayad utpadyate / na tu vartamānanīlālambanavijñānavat tu taj jñānaṃ saṃnihitavastvāk
children.translated_text: the knowledge that arises in them arises constructing such a form of the object. But that knowledge does not arise conforming to the form of a present object, like a consciousness apprehending present blue.
For [if it did], the object of that knowledge would have to be present.

But do <s>yogins</s> not perceive the future? They do not perceive it in the way you conceive. The future object must be in a present state [to be perceived]. But due to the special <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) impelled by the power of their resolution (<s>praṇidhi</s>),

children.text: vastusatpadārthavādino hi yāvat tasya vastuno 'stitvaṃ tāvat tathā svarūpasyaiva /

children.translated_text: When there is no apprehension of the entity's own nature,

children.text: tadāsya tad vastu sarvathābhāvāt kharaviṣāṇaprakhyam iti dvayavādānatikramād asya sarvam evābhisamīhitaṃ durghaṭaṃ jāyate /
children.translated_text: then, since that entity is completely non-existent, it would be like a donkey's horn — and since his two-fold doctrine is not transcended, all his aims become impossible to accomplish.
For one who holds that real entities [have inherent existence], as long as the existence of that entity persists, its own nature persists likewise.

children.text: niḥsvabhāvavādinas tu sarvathā vastusvarūpasyāsambhavād bhāvakalpanā dūrotsāritā / yena hy utpattavyaṃ na tasya nāstitvam

yadi hy asya nāstitvaṃ syāt tadāsya kharaviṣāṇādivad utpādo na syāt / athāsyāstitvaṃ syāt tadā vartamānasyevotpādo na syād asti cāsyotpāda iti siddho 'yam advayavādaḥ / yata evāsya nāstitvaṃ nāsti tata evānāgatadarśanam aviruddham
children.translated_text: for if it had non-existence, then, like a donkey's horn, it would never arise. But if it had [inherent] existence, then, like something already present, it would not arise. And yet it does arise — thus the doctrine of non-duality (<s>advayavāda</s>) is established. Precisely because it does not have non-existence, the perception of the future is not contradictory.
And because it does not have [inherent] existence,

children.text: evānāgatavyapadeśo 'pi sidhyati / eṣa ca laukiko vyavahāro na paramārtha iti nātraikāntenopapattir avatāryate /
children.translated_text: even the designation 'future' is established. And this is conventional usage, not ultimate — therefore, here reasoning is not applied in an absolute sense.

But for the proponent of the absence of inherent nature (<s>niḥsvabhāvavādin</s>), since the own-nature of an entity is in every way impossible, the conceptual construction of existence is far removed. For that which is to arise does not have non-existence —

children.text: buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ yad anāgate jñānaṃ tat pūrvapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānākṣiptayathārthapratipādakaśabdaśrutibalādhānāt tathāvidhadharmaśravaṇasaṃvartanīyakarmaviśeṣaprabhāvapariṇatavijñānasantānās tathākārānuviddhavijñānodayās tathāgatādhiṣṭhānāt ta

children.translated_text: comprehending that
meaning,

children.text: mānā yathārthaṃ pratipadyante / kālāntareṇa ca tam arthaṃ vartamānībhūtaṃ tathaivāvagacchantīty evam anāgate buddhānāṃ jñānaṃ vyavasthāpyate / na tu pūrvadharmasvabhāvavyavasthitās te kiṃcit paśyanty udāharanti cety alaṃ prasaṅgena /
children.translated_text: they comprehend it as it truly is. And after a time, perceiving that very meaning having become present, they understand it exactly so — thus is the knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s> regarding the future established. But it is not that those established in the nature of prior <s>dharmas</s> see anything and then declare it — enough with this digression.

children.text: Sentence or paragraph continues on the following page

children.translated_text: As for the knowledge of the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> regarding the future — through the power of hearing words that truthfully communicate [the teaching], impelled by previous vows and blessings, the mental continua of beings matured by the efficacy of special <s>karma</s> conducive to hearing such <s>dharma</s>, produce consciousnesses penetrated by such forms, and through the blessing of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
Thus, for the proponent of the existence of future entities, the perception of the future is impossible.

children.text: api ca / yasyānāgato 'rthaḥ svarūpato 'sti tasya na tad dūre syāt
asti cāsya dūratvam / dūraṃ dharmāḥ katame
children.translated_text: And yet it is far away. 'Which <s>dharmas</s> are far?'
'The
past and the future.' 'Which <s>dharmas</s> are near?'

children.text: pratyutpannā ity abhyupagamād anāgatam asya dūre
children.translated_text: 'The present' — since this is accepted, the future is far from it.

children.text: tac cāsya dūratvam ayuktam iti pratipādayann āha //
children.translated_text: And demonstrating that this distance is unreasonable [for the realist], he says:
Moreover, for one whose future object exists by its own nature, it would not be far away.

children.text: vidyate 'nāgataṃ yasya dūraṃ tasya na vidyate //
children.translated_text: For one to whom the future exists, distance does not exist.
The intention is: because the present is [by definition] existing [i.e., present].

children.text: yaś cānena kalyāṇamitrasamparkadharmaśravaṇendriyaparipākādikād bhāvinaḥ pratyayād dānaśīlādyātmako dharmaḥ so 'py anāgatārthasadbhāvavāditvād

children.translated_text: exists [already]. In that case:

And the <s>dharma</s>, consisting of generosity, moral conduct, and such, which arises from future conditions such as contact with a spiritual friend, hearing the <s>dharma</s>, maturation of faculties, and so on — that too, since [the opponent] holds the existence of future objects,

children.text: dharmo yady akṛto 'py asti niyamo jāyate vṛthā //
children.translated_text: If the <s>dharma</s> exists even when not performed, then discipline (<s>niyama</s>) arises in vain.

children.text: yadartham asya kāyavāṅmanasāṃ saṃyamaḥ sa dharmo 'syākṛta evāstīti tadupārjanāya niyamaśramo 'sya vṛthā / tena vināpi tasya sambhavāt /
Sentence or paragraph continues on the following page

children.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> for whose sake there is restraint of body, speech, and mind — if it exists even without being performed, then the effort of discipline for its acquisition is in vain, since it is possible even without that.

children.text: athāsya tena niyamena tasya dharmasya kaścid viśeṣo niṣpādyate sa eva viśeṣaḥ pūrvam asan paścāt kriyata iti vyāhanyate 'sya tarhi sadbhāvavāditvam iti pratipādayann āha //
children.translated_text: But if some distinction of that <s>dharma</s> is produced by that discipline — that very distinction, not existing before and being produced afterward, contradicts his thesis of [pre-]existence. Demonstrating this, he says:
then [pre-]existence of the effect is impossible.
Or if even a small [part] must be produced,

children.text: api ca yasyānityāḥ saṃskārā ity abhyupagamas tasyādhvatraye 'py avyabhicārād anityatāyā yad anityatvaṃ tasya pūr

children.translated_text: and
later phases, must certainly involve non-existence.

children.text: evaṃ hy asyānityatvaṃ sidhyate / athodayāt pūrvāparayor apy avasthayor asyāstitvaṃ syāt tadāsya
children.translated_text: For thus its impermanence is established. But if it had existence in the states both before and after arising, then it would
become
permanent
. But if he accepts impermanence, then for him:

Moreover, for one who accepts that 'conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are impermanent,' since impermanence does not deviate in any of the three times — the impermanence of that [entity], in both its earlier
When there is impermanence, how can there be [pre-]existence of the effect?
CHAPTER XII
Through cessation

children.text: vṛttyā mokṣāvāptir iti niścayaḥ / yadā caivaṃ sarvatyāgena sarvapāṣaṇḍināṃ nirvāṇam abhimataṃ tadā na kiṃcin mayātrāpūrvam upacaritaṃ yad vaimukhyakāraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: , the attainment of liberation — this is the settled conclusion. And when thus, through the relinquishment of everything, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is accepted by all ascetic sects, then nothing novel has been introduced by me here that should be a cause for aversion.
For

children.text: avet / yeṣām eva hi padārthānāṃ nirvāṇe punar apravṛttyā nirvṛttir abhisamīhitā teṣām eva mayā naiḥsvābhāvyapratipādanapareṇa śā
children.translated_text: of those very entities whose non-recurrence in <s>nirvāṇa</s> is the desired cessation, I, through this <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) devoted to establishing the absence of inherent nature,
have
accomplished the clearing of the thorns of wrong views from the path leading to the city of
<s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: tat kim iti hṛdi bhayam asad ālikhya bhavān bibhe
children.translated_text: So why, painting a non-existent fear upon your heart, do you tremble?

children.text: ti / ādhīyatāṃ manaḥparitoṣaḥ kriyatām ātmasād ayaṃ dhar
children.translated_text: Let satisfaction be established in the mind; let this <s>dharma</s> be made your own;
let
the discourse on the removal of defiling things be planted in the heart.

children.text: nanu ca yadi sarvapāṣaṇḍinām apy ayam evābhiprāyo yad uta sarvatyāgena nirvāṇam iti kaḥ punar bhavatas tīrthikānāṃ ca viśeṣaḥ / ayaṃ viśeṣo yat tīrthikānāṃ sarvatyāgābhi

children.translated_text: for the relinquishment
of everything, but not the exposition of the method for total relinquishment.
And when the method for total relinquishment has not been taught:

But if the intention of all ascetic sects is indeed this — that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is through the relinquishment of everything — then what difference is there between you and the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist philosophers)? This is the difference: for the <s>tīrthikas</s>, there is only the aspiration
relinquishment?
What will he accomplish in relinquishment — he who does not know the method of

children.text: sarvatyāgāśaye 'pi sthitas tīrthikamatāvalambī tyāgopāyānabhijñaḥ kiṃ tyāgaṃ kariṣyati / yan na jānāti sarvadharmasvabhāvaśūnyatālakṣaṇaṃ sarvatyāgopāyaṃ paramārthasatyam / ata eva //
children.translated_text: Even one who abides in the aspiration for total relinquishment, relying on <s>tīrthika</s> doctrines, ignorant of the method of relinquishment — what relinquishment will he accomplish? Since he does not know the ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>), which is the method of total relinquishment, characterized by the emptiness of inherent nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore:

children.text: śivam anyatra nāstīti nūnaṃ tenoktavān muniḥ //
children.translated_text: The sage said 'peace is not [to be found] elsewhere' — surely for this very reason.

children.text: ihaikaḥ prathamaśramaṇa iha dvitīyo yāvac caturthaḥ / śūnyāḥ parapravādāḥ śramaṇair ity amunaivābhisaṃdhinā muninaivam u
ktam iti niścīyate / asmād eva ca sarvatyāgopāyasamākhyānāt sarvatraiva bhagavato buddhasya jñānapravṛttyavyāghātena yathārthaśāstṛtvaṃ pratīyate /
children.translated_text: is established. And from this very exposition of the means of complete renunciation, it is understood that the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching is truthful everywhere, since the operation of his knowledge is unobstructed.

children.text: Sentence or paragraph continues on the following page

children.translated_text: Here, the first <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), here the second, up to the fourth — 'the claims of other schools are empty of [true] ascetics' — with this very intention, the sage said thus.

children.text: tīrthikānāṃ ca sarvatyāgopāyasamākhyānasāmarthyavaikalyenetaratrāpi padārthajāte2 viparyastavijñānatāsiddhatvān na sādhyā /
children.translated_text: And because the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) lack the capacity to expound the means of complete renunciation, even with respect to other categories of things, their claim to non-erroneous cognition cannot be established, since their cognition is proven to be erroneous.

children.text: nanu ca tavāpy aparyantatvāj jñeyasyātīndriyeṣv artheṣūpadiṣṭeṣv asamakṣatvāt te
ṣāṃ saṃśaya eva jāyate kim asāv artho yathopadiṣṭas tathaivāho svid anyatheti / na hi tadviṣayaṃ niścayakāraṇam astīti / tatrāpy ucyate //
children.translated_text: doubt alone arises regarding them — 'Is that meaning exactly as taught, or is it otherwise?' For there is no cause of certainty regarding those [supersensible] matters. To that also it is replied:
But [the objection is raised:] for you too, since the knowable is unlimited, and since the matters taught concerning supersensible objects are not directly accessible,
One who has doubt regarding the supersensible matters taught by the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: ihaiva pratyayas tena kartavyaḥ śūnyatāṃ prati //
children.translated_text: should gain conviction right here [in this life] with respect to <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness).

children.text: na hi sarve bhāvāḥ pratyakṣajñānagamyā anumānagamyā api vidyante / śakyaṃ cātrānumānaṃ kartuṃ dṛṣṭāntasadbhāvāt / iha tyā
gopāyaḥ sarvadharmasvabhāvaśūnyatā / sā cāśakyā kenacid anyathātvam āsādayitum

children.translated_text: And this is a subtle matter — though ever-present, it is not directly accessible to all people.

children.text: tasya copapattyā sarvadharmasvabhāvagrāhavinivāraṇamukhenopapāditā yathāvattā / atraiva tāvad āsthīyatāṃ niścayaḥ / kim evam evaitad utāho 'nyatheti / athātrāsti kiṃcid aniścayakāraṇaṃ tad upadiśyatāṃ yadi tan na nirākṛtam u
children.translated_text: And its truth has been demonstrated through reasoning, by way of removing the grasping at the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. Let certainty be established right here — is this exactly so, or is it otherwise? If there is any cause for uncertainty in this matter, let it be pointed out — if it has not been refuted by the

children.text: ktavakṣyamāṇaprakaraṇapratipāditaviniścayena / na ca śakyam anena svalpam apy aniścayakāraṇaṃ kiṃcid abhidhātum iti
children.translated_text: determination established in the foregoing and forthcoming chapters. And since not even the slightest cause for uncertainty can be stated by this [objector],
this example is
indeed established.

children.text: tataś cānyad apy asamakṣārthapratipādakavacanaṃ bhagavato yathārtham iti pratīyatāṃ svanayenaiva tathāgatopadiṣṭatvāt svabhāvaśūnyatārthābhidhāyakavacanavad iti kuto buddhokteṣu paro'kṣeṣu saṃśayāvakāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, let it be accepted that any other statement of the Blessed One that conveys supersensible matters is also true, since it was taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s> through his own method, just like the statement that conveys the meaning of emptiness of intrinsic nature — so where is there room for doubt regarding the supersensible matters taught by the <s>Buddha</s>?

For not all entities are accessible through direct perception — some are accessible through inference. And inference can be made here, since a valid example exists. Here, the means of renunciation is the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. And that cannot be made otherwise by anyone.

children.text: na ca tathāgatavat tīrthikānām api śakyam a

viparītārthābhidhāyitvam avasātuṃ teṣāṃ dṛṣṭa eva viparyastatvāt / tathāhy asya lokasya tair nityakāraṇapūrvikā pravṛttir upadiśyate / sā cāśakyapratipādyā dṛṣṭaviruddhā copapattiviruddhā cety evam //
children.translated_text: meaning cannot be established, since they are seen to be erroneous in directly observable matters. For they teach that the functioning of this world is preceded by a permanent cause, and that is incapable of being demonstrated, being contradicted by what is observed and contradicted by reasoning. Thus:
And unlike the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>tīrthikas</s>' [claim to] conveying non-erroneous

children.text: loko 'yaṃ yena durdṛṣṭo mūḍha eva paratra saḥ //
children.translated_text: One by whom this world is wrongly seen — that one is indeed deluded with regard to the hereafter as well.

children.text: na hi sampūrṇe candramasi vyāhatadarśanasāmarthyo dhruvam arundhatīṃ vā paśyatīti sambhāvyam
tadvad ayaṃ tīrthiko lokasya sattvabhājanākhyasya he
children.translated_text: Likewise, this <s>tīrthika</s>, being confused about the cause-and-effect [relationship] of the world — comprising sentient beings and the environment —

children.text: tuphalavyāmūḍhatvāt sthūlam evārthaṃ tāvad yadā na samyag īkṣate tadā katham ayam atisūkṣmaṃ vidūradeśakālavyavahitaṃ saprabhedam arthaṃ jñāsyatīti sambhāvayituṃ śakyam / tad imaṃ tīrthikaṃ svayam atyantaviparyāsitadarśanaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇājalavad anupāsanīyaṃ tattvadarśanāmalajalapipāsavaḥ saṃsārādhvapariśramaklamāpanodanāya
children.translated_text: when he does not even rightly perceive a gross matter, how can it be supposed that he will know a matter that is extremely subtle, separated by distant place and time, and differentiated? Therefore, this <s>tīrthika</s>, whose view is utterly perverted, should not be resorted to — like the water of a mirage — by those who thirst for the pure water of truth-vision, for the removal of the exhaustion of wandering on the path of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
For it is not to be supposed that one whose capacity of vision is impaired with respect to the full moon can reliably perceive even <s>Arundhatī</s> [the faintest star].

children.text: // vañcitās te bhaviṣyanti suciraṃ ye 'nuyānti tam //
children.translated_text: Those who follow him for a long time will be deceived.

children.text: aparyavasānāparakoṭike saṃsāre te vata vañcitā bhaviṣyanti ye yathārthaśāstāraṃ
buddhaṃ bhagavantam avadhūya dṛṣṭādṛṣṭapadārthasvabhāvavyāmūḍhaṃ mokṣakāmatayā tīrthikam anuyāsyanti /
children.translated_text: having rejected the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, the teacher of truth, will follow a <s>tīrthika</s> who is confused about the nature of both seen and unseen things, out of desire for liberation.
In <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is endless and without a further limit, those indeed will be deceived who,
that very
<s>tīrthika</s> of perverted views? Out of fear of hearing the teaching of the <s>dharma</s> of emptiness of intrinsic nature.
That fear [arises from the thought:]
But why do these seekers of liberation follow

children.text: nāsty ahaṃ na bhaviṣyāmi na me 'sti na bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: 'I do not exist, I shall not exist; [what is] mine does not exist, [and it] shall not exist.'

children.text: ata eva kalyāṇamitraparigrahāt sucirābhyastam api bhāvasvabhāvābhinive
children.translated_text: For this very reason, through the guidance of a virtuous spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), having abandoned the attachment to the intrinsic nature of [inherent] existence, even though long habituated, as one would discard
filth —
It is due to the terror arising from grasping at this. And this [terror comes] from the long habituation to <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense) and <s>mamakāra</s> (possessiveness).

children.text: svayaṃ ye yānti nirvāṇaṃ te kurvanti suduṣkaram /
children.translated_text: those who themselves go to <s>nirvāṇa</s> accomplish what is supremely difficult.

children.text: buddho bhagavān svayaṃ bhūtvā svayam eva nirvāṇapuram upayāti

children.translated_text: Of that one who accomplishes such difficult deeds,
The Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, having himself become [awakened], himself proceeds to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: gantuṃ notsahate netuḥ pṛṣṭhato 'py asato manaḥ //
children.translated_text: the mind of the unworthy does not dare to follow even behind the guide to go [to <s>nirvāṇa</s>].

children.text: na kevalam asatām ahaṅkaramamakaravyavasthitānāṃ svayam eva nirvāṇaṃ gantuṃ mano notsahate
api khalu yathopavarṇitasya netuḥ pṛṣṭhato 'py asyāsato nirvā
children.translated_text: but indeed the mind of this unworthy one does not experience the courage to go to <s>nirvāṇa</s>
even following behind the afore-described guide.
Not only does the mind of the unworthy — those established in <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense) and <s>mamakāra</s> (possessiveness) — not dare to go to <s>nirvāṇa</s> by itself,

children.text: kasmāt punar asya netuḥ pṛṣṭhato 'py asataḥ pudgalasya nirvāṇaṃ gantuṃ mano notsahate

It is not the case that what is form is itself the pot — the identity of form and pot is not possible. For if there were identity of form and pot, then wherever there is form, there would be a pot, and so there would be a pot in form everywhere. Being,

children.text: yor dṛṣṭvā bhāvād anyo ghaṭo bhavaty evam eva vailakṣaṇyād ghaṭād api kim arthaṃ bhāvo 'nyo na bhavi
children.translated_text: then by the same token, because of the difference of characteristics, why would Being not also be other than the pot? And then, yet another otherness — having the characteristic of recurrence — would need to be conceived as the ground for the operation of the cognition and word 'other.'
But that is not required, since the operation of the cognition and word 'other' is established
merely by

children.text: nipravṛttinimittam anyatvam aparam anupravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ na kalpayitavyam / vailakṣaṇyād evānyabuddhidhvanipravṛttisiddheḥ
children.translated_text: the difference of characteristics.

children.text: Sentence or paragraph continues on the following page

children.translated_text: Since Being (<s>bhāva</s>) has the characteristic of recurring in pot-substances and the like, it is the universal. And since the pot has the characteristic of exclusion [from other things], it is a particular. If, seeing the difference of characteristics between

children.text: kalpyate cāparam anyatvam iti nāsti tarhi bhāvaghaṭayor vailakṣaṇyāpekṣam anyatvam

children.translated_text: And consequently, what was stated —
If yet another otherness is conceived, then there is no otherness of Being and pot that depends on a difference of characteristics.

children.text: vailakṣaṇyaṃ dvayor dṛṣṭvā bhāvād anyo ghaṭa
children.translated_text: 'Having seen the difference of characteristics between the two, the pot is other than Being' —
that is not valid.

children.text: yathā ca bhāvo 'nupravṛttilakṣaṇatvād ghaṭād anya evam anyatvam apy anupravṛttilakṣaṇatvād ghaṭā

children.translated_text: And that [further otherness]

children.text: na ca tasyānyatvasyāparam anyatvam anyabuddhidhvanipravṛttinimittam asti / yadi syād anyatvānām aparyavasānadoṣaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: of that otherness — there is no further otherness as the ground for the operation of the cognition and word 'other.' If there were, there would be the fault of an infinite regress of othernesses.
And just as Being, because of having the characteristic of recurrence, is other than the pot, so too otherness itself, because of having the characteristic of recurrence, would be other than the pot.

children.text: tadvad evānyatrāpi sambhāvyatām ity alam anyatvenākiṃcitkareṇa parikalpitena / asati cānyatve nāsti kutaścit kasyacid anyatvam iti siddham /
children.translated_text: then let that be accepted elsewhere as well — and enough with this pointless, conceptually fabricated otherness. And in the absence of otherness, it is established that nothing is other than anything.
But if the cognition of otherness arises regarding otherness even without [a further] otherness,

children.text: api cedaṃ cintyate kiṃbhūtāyāḥ sattāyā anyatvena yogo

children.translated_text: Is it with one that is [already] other, or with one that is not other?

children.text: yady anyabhūtāyās tadā vyartho 'nyatvena yogaḥ / athānanyabhūtāyā
children.translated_text: If with one that is [already] other, then the connection with otherness is superfluous. But if with one that is not other,
then

children.text: evam api viruddhenānanyatvena yogād anyatvena yogo na prāpnoti / anyatvābhāvāc ca ghaṭād anyo bhāva iti na yujyate / tataś ca loke viparyāsaṃ pramānīkṛtya ghaṭatvarūpam eva sadbuddhidhvanipravṛttinimittatvād bhāva iti vyavasthāpyate / tasya ca
children.translated_text: even so, since the connection is with non-otherness, which is contradictory, the connection with otherness does not follow. And since otherness is absent, it is not tenable that Being is other than the pot. Therefore, in the world, taking worldly error as authoritative, it is the very form of pot-ness that, being the ground for the operation of the cognition and word 'existent,' is established as 'Being.' And that [pot-ness],

children.text: rūpāc caturdhāvicāryamāṇasya nāsti svabhāva iti / tattvavidapekṣayālātacakrādivat svabhāvaśūnyo ghaṭa iti siddham /
children.translated_text: when analyzed fourfold from [the perspective of] form, has no own-nature. Thus, from the standpoint of one who knows reality, it is established that the pot is empty of own-nature, like a fire-wheel.
Moreover, this is to be considered: with Being of what kind should there be a connection of otherness?

children.text: atrāha / vidyata eva ghaṭo guṇāśrayatvāt / na hy asad guṇāśrayo dṛṣṭaḥ / bhavati ca guṇāśrayo ghaṭa eko ghaṭo dvau ghaṭāv iti / ekatvādayo guṇapadārthasaṃgṛhītā ghaṭaś ca dravyam

children.translated_text: And it is possible for qualities to have a substance as their substrate.

children.text: ato guṇāśrayatvād asty eva ghaṭa iti / atrocyate / tvanmatena //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because it is a substrate of qualities, the pot does indeed exist. To this it is replied: According to your view:

Here one objects: The pot does indeed exist, because it is a substrate of qualities. For a non-existent thing is not seen to be a substrate of qualities. And the pot is a substrate of qualities — 'one pot,' 'two pots,' etc. Oneness and the like are included in the category of quality, and the pot is a substance.

children.text: eko yadi ghaṭo neṣṭo ghaṭo 'py eko na jāyate //
children.translated_text: If oneness is not accepted as the pot, then the pot too does not become one.

children.text: padārthabhedād yady eko ghaṭo na bhavatīti manyase ghaṭo 'pi tarhy eko na bhavati
yathaikatvam ekasaṃkhyā ghaṭo na bhavaty evaṃ dravyatvenaikasaṃkhyāyāḥ pṛthagbhūtatvād ghaṭo 'py eko na bhavati
children.translated_text: Just as oneness — the number one — is not the pot, so too, since the number one is a separate entity qua substance, the pot too is not one.

children.text: dvitvād iti bhāvaḥ / api cāsya ghaṭasyaikarūpasyaikasaṃkhyā parikalpetā
children.translated_text: The meaning is: because of duality. Moreover, should the number one of this pot be conceived for the pot as having a single form

children.text: nekarūpasya vā / yady ekarūpasya tadā vyarthaivaikatvakalpanā / athānekarūpasya tadāpi viruddhatvād ayuktaiva
children.translated_text: or as having multiple forms? If for one having a single form, then the conception of oneness is simply superfluous. But if for one having multiple forms, then it is untenable because of contradiction.
Therefore, in the world, the conception of oneness should be understood as belonging to the very form of the pot, with no separate real entity present.
If you think that the pot is not [identical with] oneness due to the difference of categories, then the pot too does not become one.

children.text: atha dravyāśrayiṇo guṇā iti kṛtvaikatvayogād ghaṭa evaiko bhavati na tv ekatvaṃ

children.translated_text: the pot—
to this it is replied:
Now, if [one argues that] because qualities inhere in substance, the pot itself becomes one through connection with oneness, but oneness does not become

children.text: na cāyaṃ samayor yogas tenāpy eko na jāyate //
children.translated_text: And this connection is not between equals; therefore, even through that, [the pot] does not become one.
not between unequals.

children.text: Sentence or paragraph continues on the following page

children.translated_text: For connection (<s>yoga</s>) occurs only between equals,

children.text: tatraiko guṇo dṛṣṭo ghaṭaś ca dravyam
dravyaguṇayoś ca samatā yasmān na bhavati tasmāt tayor yoga eva na bhavati
children.translated_text: And since there is no equality between substance and quality, therefore there is simply no connection between them.

children.text: yogābhāvāt tatra yad iṣṭam ekatyayogād ghaṭa evaiko bhavatīti tan na / yadi cātra yogo dṛṣṭas tadaikenāpi ghaṭasya yogaḥ syād ghaṭenāpy ekasya / sa ca naivaṃ bhavatīti yoga evānayor nopapadyate / yogābhāvāc ca naivaiko ghaṭo bhavatīti na ghaṭo 'py eka iti / tad atra pūrvārdhena kārikāyā yo
children.translated_text: Since there is no connection, the desired claim that 'the pot itself becomes one through connection with oneness' is not valid. Moreover, if such a connection were observed, then oneness too would have a connection with the pot, and the pot with oneness. But this does not happen — therefore the connection between these two is simply untenable. And since there is no connection, the pot does not become one — thus the pot too is not one. Now, by the first half of the verse, a refutation was stated granting the connection;

children.text: uttarārdhena tu yogāsambhave dūṣaṇam uktam / apiśabdaś ca dūṣaṇakāraṇasamuccayārtho draṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: by the second half, a refutation was stated showing the impossibility of the connection. And the word 'api' ('also') should be understood as indicating the accumulation of reasons for refutation.
Here, oneness is a quality and the pot is a substance.

children.text: api cedam ayuktataraṃ parasamaye dṛśyate / yad dravyāśrayiṇo guṇā vyavasthāpyante na guṇāśrayiṇo viśeṣaguṇāḥ / yujyate ca guṇānām api guṇāśrayitvam / iha yatparimāṇo ghaṭas tadāśrayeṇāpi rūpeṇa tāvataiva bhavitavyam / tataś ca dravyavad rūpasyāpi mahattvaṃ prāpno

children.translated_text: greatness. Therefore:

Moreover, this is even more untenable in the opponent's system: that qualities are established as inhering in substance, but particular qualities are not established as inhering in [other] qualities. Yet it is proper for qualities too to be substrates of qualities. For the form that is the substrate of a pot must be of the same extent as the pot itself. And thus, like a substance, form too would have

children.text: yāvad dravyaṃ yadā rūpaṃ tadā rūpaṃ mahan na kim //
children.translated_text: When form is coextensive with the substance, then why would form not be great?

children.text: yadā yāvad dravyaṃ yāvān dravyasyāyāmavistārātmakaḥ sanniveśas tāvad rūpaṃ rūpasyāpi tāvān evāyāmavistārātmakaḥ sanniveśa iti pareṇābhyupagamyate tadā niyatam aṇumahati dravye rūpeṇāpi tatrāṇumahattā bhavitavyam / tat kiṃ nu khalv atra kāraṇaṃ yad dravyavad rūpasyāṇumahattve neṣyete /
children.translated_text: When it is accepted by the opponent that the extent of a substance is [equal to] its spatial configuration consisting of length and breadth, and that the extent of form (<s>rūpa</s>) too has exactly the same spatial configuration of length and breadth — then, necessarily, in a small or large substance, the form too must be correspondingly small or large there. So what then is the reason that smallness and largeness of form are not accepted just as [they are] for substance?

children.text: paṃ guṇo 'ṇutvaṃ mahattvam api ca guṇa eva na ca guṇe guṇasya sanniveśo bhavatīti samaya eṣo 'smākam / tataś ca yady api yāvad dravyaṃ rūpam api tāvad eva tathāpi siddhāntavirodhabhayād rūpasyāṇutvamahattve na sta iti / ucyate //
children.translated_text: is a quality (<s>guṇa</s>); smallness and largeness are also just qualities; and a quality does not have a spatial configuration within a quality — this is our doctrinal convention. And therefore, even though form is as extensive as the substance, yet out of fear of contradicting our own doctrine, we do not accept smallness and largeness of form.' It is replied:
If one were to say: 'Form

children.text: samayo jāyate vācyaḥ prativādy aparo yadi //
children.translated_text: A doctrinal convention must be stated [only] if the opponent is [from one's own school].

children.text: yadi hi tava svayūthya eva prativādī syāt taṃ nivartayituṃ yuktaṃ tava siddhāntābhidhānaṃ tasya tad bādhi

tum asāmarthyāt / yadā tu prativādī paras taṃ prati siddhāntavirodhodbhāvanam akiṃcitkaraṃ siddhāntanirākaraṇapravṛttatvāt tasya / yuktilokavirodhodbhāvanaṃ tu taṃ prati jyāyaḥ / taddvāreṇa tasya nivārayituṃ śakyatvāt / tasmād aparihāra evāyaṃ yad idam āgamavirodhodbhāvanam iti sa evāvicalo doṣa iti nāsti bhāvaghaṭayor anyatvam / tad atra
children.translated_text: But when the opponent is an outsider, the invocation of doctrinal contradiction against him is futile, since he is engaged in the refutation of [your] doctrine. The invocation of contradiction with reasoning and common experience against him would be superior, since he can be restrained through that. Therefore, this is no answer at all — this invocation of scriptural contradiction. That very same unshakeable fault [remains] — therefore, there is no difference between <s>bhāva</s> (being/existence) and the pot. And here,

children.text: sattānyatvapratiṣedhenānyeṣām api ghaṭatvādīnāṃ sāmānyaviśeṣāṇāṃ pratiṣedho vijñeyaḥ / saṃkhyāvat sāmānyaguṇānāṃ mahattvavad viśeṣāṇām iti /
children.translated_text: through the denial of the otherness of <s>sattā</s> (existence), the denial of other [categories] too — such as <s>ghaṭatva</s> (pot-ness) and so forth, both universals and particulars — should be understood: of universals like number, and of particulars like largeness.
For if your opponent were from your own school, it would be appropriate for you to state a doctrinal convention to restrain him, since he would be unable to refute it.

children.text: atrāha / ukto bhāvasya ghaṭādibhyo 'nyatvapratiṣedhaḥ / ghaṭasya tu svabhāvāpratiṣedhād asty eva svarūpato ghaṭākhyo bhāva iti / atrocyate //
children.translated_text: Here one objects: the denial of the otherness of <s>bhāva</s> from the pot and such has been stated. But since the own-nature of the pot has not been denied, there does indeed exist an entity called 'pot' by its own nature. To this it is replied:
where —
Even by means of a defining characteristic, the establishment of the definiendum is not found
there, apart from number and such, no entity exists.

children.text: iha ghaṭasattvayor vyāvṛttyanuvṛttilakṣaṇaṃ bruvatā ghaṭasya vyāvṛttilakṣaṇaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ pareṇa

tad amunā lakṣaṇenāpi lakṣyasya nāsti siddhiḥ / na hi vyāvrttimātreṇa śakyaṃ vastusvarūpaṃ nirdhārayituṃ yal lakṣyatayā setsyati / ekas tāvad guṇatvād ghaṭo na bhavati / aṇur mahad iti rūpādayaś ca guṇatvād eva ghaṭā
children.translated_text: But even by this defining characteristic, there is no establishment of the definiendum. For by mere exclusion alone, it is not possible to determine the own-nature of a real thing that would be established as the definiendum. First, a pot does not exist on account of being a single quality. And form and the rest — which may be small or large — do not become called 'pot' precisely because they are qualities. <s>Sattā</s> (existence) too, being a universal in substance, quality, and action, is not a pot.

children.text: khyā na bhavanti / sattāpi dravyaguṇakarmasu sāmānyād ghaṭo na bhavati / tad ayaṃ saṃkhyāṇumahadrūpādibhyo vyāvartamāna itthaṃ svabhāva iti na śakyaṃ vyavasthāpayitum / tad evaṃ yatra paravādipakṣe lakṣaṇenāpi lakṣyasya ghaṭasvarūpasya nāsti siddhis tatra pakṣe saṃkhyādivyatirekeṇa siddhasvarūpeṇa ghaṭākhyo bhāvo na vidyate / tataś ca svabhāvaśūnyo ghaṭa iti siddham /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this [pot], which is distinguished from number, smallness, largeness, form, and such, cannot be established as having such-and-such an own-nature. Thus, in the opponent's position where even by the defining characteristic there is no establishment of the definiendum — the own-nature of the pot — in that position, apart from number and such having established own-natures, no entity called 'pot' exists. And therefore, it is established that the pot is empty of inherent nature.
Here, the opponent, in stating the defining characteristic of the pot and <s>sattā</s> in terms of exclusion and inclusion, has established the pot's defining characteristic as exclusion.

children.text: athavā saṃkhyārūpādayo ghaṭasya lakṣaṇaṃ tair lakṣyamāṇatvād ghaṭo lakṣyaḥ
tasya lakṣaṇenāpi pṛthak svarūpasiddhir aśakyā kartum / saṃkhyādivyatirekeṇa tatsvarūpasyānupalabhyamānatvāt
children.translated_text: Its establishment as having an own-nature separate from the defining characteristics is impossible to effect, because its own-nature is not apprehended apart from number and such.
Alternatively, number, form, and such are the defining characteristics of the pot; being defined by them, the pot is the definiendum.

children.text: yadi hi tal lakṣyaṃ svarūpaṃ labhate tadā niyataṃ saṃkhyādivyatirekeṇa gṛhyetedaṃ tat saṃkhyāvyatiriktaṃ ghaṭasvarūpam idaṃ punar asya saṃkhyādikaṃ lakṣaṇam iti

children.translated_text: But this is not so; therefore:

For if that definiendum were to possess an own-nature, then it would certainly be apprehended apart from number and such — [one could say:] 'this is the own-nature of the pot, distinct from number; and this is its defining characteristic, namely number and such.'

children.text: lakṣaṇenāpi lakṣyasya yatra siddhir na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Even by means of a defining characteristic, the establishment of the definiendum is not found where —
there, apart from number and such, no entity exists.
the pot does not exist by its own nature.
Thus

children.text: uktas tāval lakṣyalakṣaṇayor anyatvapratiṣedhaḥ / yeṣāṃ tu rūpādibhir ghaṭasyaikyam iti siddhāntas tatpratiṣedhāyedam ucyate //
children.translated_text: The denial of the otherness of the definiendum and the defining characteristic has been stated. But for those whose doctrine is that the pot is identical with form and the rest — to refute that, this is said:

children.text: ghaṭasya na bhavaty aikyam apṛthaktvād dhi lakṣaṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The pot cannot have unity, because of non-difference from its defining characteristics;
since the pot is absent in each one [of them], plurality too is not established.

children.text: rūpādīni khalu nānālakṣaṇāni yeṣāṃ tair apṛthaktvaṃ ghaṭasyeṣṭaṃ teṣāṃ rūpādibhir lakṣaṇair apṛthaktvād ghaṭasyaikyaṃ nopapadyate bahubhir ananyatvāt /
children.translated_text: For those who accept the non-difference of the pot from its defining characteristics, namely form and such, which have diverse characteristics — because of non-difference from those defining characteristics (form and such), the unity of the pot is not established, since it would be non-different from many [things].

children.text: syāt tatra mataṃ yadi ghaṭasyaikyaṃ na bhavati
hanta bahutvaṃ prāptam iti / atrocyate / yasmād rūpādiṣv ekaikasmin ghaṭasyābhāvo dṛṣṭas tasmād bahutvam api nāstīti /
children.translated_text: well then, plurality would follow. To this it is replied: since the absence of the pot is observed in each one of form and such, plurality too does not exist.
One might think: if the pot does not have unity,

children.text: yadi rūpādibhir lakṣaṇair apṛthaktvād ghaṭasyaikyaṃ nāsti teṣāṃ parasparasaṃyogād ghaṭasyaikyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti / atrocyate //
children.translated_text: If the pot does not have unity because of non-difference from its defining characteristics (form and such), then the pot will have unity through the mutual conjunction of those [characteristics]. To this it is replied:
Here one objects:

children.text: na hy asparśavato nāma yogaḥ sparśavatā saha
children.translated_text: For there is no conjunction of that which is intangible with that which is tangible;

children.text: rūpādīnām ato yogaḥ sarvathāpi na yujyate //
children.translated_text: therefore, the conjunction of form and the rest is in no way possible.
The tangible (<s>spraṣṭavya</s>) alone is tangible, because of being graspable by the tactile sense organ.

children.text: tena sparśavatā spraṣṭavyena rūpagandharasānām asparśavatāṃ yogaḥ saṃyogaḥ saṃsparśo na sambhavati
children.translated_text: The conjunction — that is, contact or meeting — of form, smell, and taste, which are intangible, with the tangible [quality of touch], is not possible,
just as [there is no conjunction] of a pot with space.

children.text: Sentence or paragraph continues on the following page

children.translated_text: Here, 'touch' means contact, i.e., graspability by the tactile sense organ; 'tangible' means that which possesses touch.

children.text: yata etad evaṃ rūpādīnām ato yogaḥ sarvaprakāraṃ na sambhavati / yadā ca na sambhavati tadānyonyasaṃsparśakṛtād rūpādīnāṃ viśeṣāt samudāyanibandhano ghaṭa iti yad uktaṃ tan na yuktam /
children.translated_text: Since this is so, the conjunction of form and the rest is in no way possible. And when it is not possible, the statement that the pot is based on a collection arising from the mutual contact of form and the rest is not reasonable.

children.text: py anyonyasaṃsparśena tatsamudāya eva ghaṭa iti syād
children.translated_text: mutual contact, the mere collection of those [qualities] is the pot.
This too is not [the case],
because:
But [one might say:] even without

children.text: ghaṭasyāvayavo rūpaṃ tena tāvan na tad ghaṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Form is a part of the pot; therefore that [form] is not the pot.

children.text: yasmād avayavī nāsti tena nāvayavo 'pi tat //
children.translated_text: Since a whole does not exist, therefore a part too is not that [pot].

children.text: rūpādisamudāyarūpasya ghaṭasya pratyekaṃ rūpādayo 'vayavabhūtatvād ghaṭavyapadeśabhājo na bhavanti / ghaṭo 'vayavy avayavāś ca rūpādaya iti rūpaṃ tāvad avayavatvād ghaṭo na prāpnoti / yathā ca rūpam evaṃ

children.translated_text: smell and the rest should be stated.

Since the pot has the nature of a collection of form and such, individually, form and the rest, being parts, do not deserve the designation 'pot.' The pot is the whole, and form and the rest are parts — thus, form, being a part, does not qualify as the pot. And just as form, so too

children.text: nanu ca rūpasyāvayavatvād asti tarhy asāv avayavī nāma kaścit / na hy avayavinirapekṣā avayavā yujyanta iti / ucyate / iha rūpādīnāṃ pratyekaṃ ghaṭatvābhāve kutaḥ kaścid avayavī / na hi rūpādivyatirekeṇāvayavī nāma paricchettuṃ pāryate / na cāparicchidyamānasvarūpasya sattvam āsthātuṃ śakyam ity asann avayavī / yasmāc cāvayavī nāsti tasmād rūpam avayavatvenāpi na sambhāvyata i
ti na sta evāvayavāvayavinau / itaś ca rūpādisamudāyo na ghaṭaḥ / yasmāt
children.translated_text: — thus neither parts nor whole exist. And furthermore, the collection of form and such is not the pot, because:

But [one objects:] since form is a part, then surely there exists some entity called the whole. For parts without reference to a whole are not reasonable. It is replied: here, when each of form and the rest individually lacks pot-ness, whence any whole? For the whole cannot be discerned apart from form and the rest. And the existence of something whose own nature cannot be discerned cannot be maintained — therefore the whole does not exist. And since the whole does not exist, form too cannot be conceived as a part
The form-ness of all forms is undifferentiated;

children.text: ekasya ghaṭasadbhāvo nānyeṣāṃ kiṃ nu kāraṇam //
children.translated_text: that one [set of forms] constitutes a pot while others do not — what is the reason for this?

children.text: sarveṣām api rūpāṇām iti rūpaskandhasaṃgṛhītatvād rūpagandhādayo rūpāṇīty ucyante / tāni rūpāṇi ghaṭa iva paṭādiṣv api santi
